changeSet.comment: catalog_collections attribute backfill walk (branches A-D above) plus the constraints that make the table true: NOT NULL and non-empty CHECK on content_type/owner_id/embedding_model, FK embedding_model -> embedding_models, CHECK + NOT NULL on lifecycle_state. Both catalog_collections (the DML target) and chunks/catalog_document_chunks/catalog_documents (read via nexus.collection_vector_stats -> nexus.live_chunks) carry FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so all four are toggled (aspects-004-1 / hygiene-001-6 precedent: toggling only the target leaves the correlated read yielding zero rows for the non-bypass migrating role) -- toggled in this order, restored in reverse (LIFO).

changeSet.author: nexus-ft04v.4
changeSet.comment: RDR-204 nexus-ft04v.4/.5 fallout: vectors-005-12/13's gc_quarantine_orphans and gc_restore_rereferenced (the CURRENT, post-RDR-191 dim-agnostic bodies -- catalog-024's original per-dim bodies were already superseded by vectors-005 before this changeset ever runs) stub-insert catalog_collections (tenant_id, name, content_type, owner_id, embedding_model, model_version) with no lifecycle_state column at all, and an empty-string fallback for content_type/owner_id/embedding_model on a non-4-segment name. Both are now illegal: lifecycle_state is NOT NULL and the three metadata columns carry a non-empty CHECK (hygiene-002-1, same changelog file). PostgreSQL enforces both against the attempted VALUES tuple of an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING BEFORE it resolves the conflict, so even a pre-existing row (registered elsewhere first) does not save an omitted/blank stub from a 23502 or CHECK violation on this exact statement. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION redefines both functions with the same signature, return shape, and sweep-gate / cross-dim-collision-guard logic as vectors-005 -- only the stub-insert VALUES lists change, to a lifecycle_state literal (quarantine for the quarantine-sibling registration; live for the origin-collection re-registration) and non-empty placeholders matching PgContainerHelper.insertCollection's Java-side "unknown stub" defaults.
